clue.text: Stenographers use it for only a limited span

definitions.meaning: the quick abbreviated script used by secretaries taking dictation
read literally, a ... covers only a small stretch, as a hand-span measures distance

explanation.surface: A remark about secretaries and a writing system good for brief stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated writing system of stenographers carries the same name as a small hand, whose span is limited.

clue.text: One who entertains a lot of people

definitions.meaning: a person who receives guests
a great multitude, as in a heavenly throng

explanation.surface: Describing a party-giver who welcomes crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A party-giver is a synonym in one sense, and a large crowd or multitude is the other sense.

clue.text: Root for a political reformer

definitions.meaning: in mathematics, the root sign or a root itself; also a word's base
someone seeking sweeping change in politics

explanation.surface: Cheering on a campaigner for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematical root sign shares the name with an extremist who wants thoroughgoing political change.

clue.text: Offer resistance it would seem

parts.note: to resist is to refuse to give in; yet to offer something is literally to extend it outward in the hand, so the phrase seems to mean both

explanation.surface: A tentative suggestion that someone is putting up a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to resist or refuse to yield, while literally it describes extending a thing as an offer.

clue.text: Eat in apparently noisy environment

parts.note: a slangy, rather onomatopoeic word for eating, suggesting munching sounds at a meal

explanation.surface: Having a meal somewhere loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for food or eating, whose sound suggests noisy munching.

clue.text: Dispute caused by mail-liner's sea crossing

definitions.text: Dispute caused by mail-liner's sea crossing

parts.words: Dispute caused by mail-liner's sea crossing
parts.note: a voyage is a sea crossing, and mail can mean armour or weapons, so a crossing of mail is a clash of weapons

explanation.surface: A quarrel arising from a postal ship's voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like letters carried by a ship, but chain mail is armour, so the crossing becomes a clash of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a fight or heated exchange, originally a bout of swordplay.

clue.text: Superhuman job for Poirot with a six-footer to question

parts.note: Hercule is the first name of Agatha Christie's detective Poirot
an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: An enormous job set for Agatha Christie's detective, who must interrogate a tall suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules performed twelve labours, so a task named after him needs enormous effort.

clue.text: Those spectacles grandpa mislaid when toasting?

definitions.text: Those spectacles grandpa mislaid when toasting?

parts.words: Those spectacles grandpa mislaid when toasting?
parts.note: an old man's spectacles are often pushed up onto his forehead and forgotten; a toast also lifts drinking vessels up

explanation.surface: Grandpa has lost his specs during a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting drinking vessels is how a toast is made, while lifted spectacles are the ones grandpa has lost on his forehead.

clue.text: Fuse leads to a charge by action-hungry spectators?

definitions.text: Fuse leads to a charge by action-hungry spectators?

parts.words: Fuse leads to a charge by action-hungry spectators?
parts.note: a fuse burns slowly toward an explosive charge, while bored spectators at a dull sporting fixture may grumble for action

explanation.surface: A fuse burns toward explosives, or restless fans complain about a dull game.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-burning cord used to ignite explosives, and also a dull sporting contest that bores spectators.

clue.text: Daily supplier of fresh garden herb to the National Trust

parts.note: fresh means new
sage is a common garden herb
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Someone who delivers herbs to a heritage charity every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' means a daily newspaper, so the definition is someone who supplies papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells newspapers, the dailies, so supplies them.

clue.text: Look! A way! But obviously you can't find it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone spots a path, then admits it cannot be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mislaid is something nobody can locate.

clue.text: Drama being staged near Ealing

parts.note: an act is a part of a drama
a play being staged is on

explanation.surface: Theatre production in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON and Ealing are neighbouring districts in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of west London lying beside Ealing.

clue.text: Area of land on the Israeli coast

definitions.meaning: a unit of land measurement of 4840 square yards
an ancient port city in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A plot of land by the Mediterranean in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A land measure shares its name with a historic Mediterranean port city in Israel.

clue.text: In Durban Tutu claims to speak for them

indicators.note: in signals that the letters run concealed within the words Durban Tutu

explanation.surface: Desmond Tutu, in Durban, claims to represent a people.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Desmond Tutu was a South African leader; the definition 'them' points to the people he claims to speak for.
explanation.definitionFit: A large family of southern African peoples, those for whom a South African leader might speak.

clue.text: Wild dog in Australia-quite literally

indicators.note: wild suggests unruly disorder, so the letters of dog and in are jumbled

explanation.surface: A feral canine down under, described exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The native feral canine of Australia, a wild dog by definition.

clue.text: What a dog may do when it spots a bird

definitions.meaning: a happy dog shakes its rear appendage
a small songbird with a long, bobbing tail

explanation.surface: A dog shakes its tail with excitement at seeing a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking its tail is a dog's gesture, and the same phrase names a small bird that bobs its tail.

clue.text: Insignificant details on the dessert menu

definitions.meaning: trivial matters, small things of no importance
a pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.surface: Fussing over minor points on a list of puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered pudding of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial matters are a synonym, and the layered British pudding is the other sense.

clue.text: A job with the French missionary

parts.note: a post is a job
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone takes up work alongside French people as a preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Early Christian missionaries, like Paul, were called by this title.

clue.text: Properties on the American Atlantic coast

parts.note: the Atlantic coast of America is its east coast, abbreviated E
the States is a name for America

explanation.surface: Houses along the eastern seaboard of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed properties, large houses with grounds, are a synonym.

clue.text: The singularity which began to change stock market in '86

definitions.meaning: the cosmic origin from a point of infinite density
the 1986 deregulation of the London Stock Exchange

explanation.surface: Linking the birth of the universe with a financial upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1986 the London Stock Exchange was deregulated in one day, nicknamed after the cosmic origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe began from a singularity in the cosmic explosion, and the London deregulation borrowed its name.

clue.text: A small guide to a simple box camera

definitions.meaning: a junior member of the Girl Guides
a cheap Kodak camera introduced in 1900

explanation.surface: Instructions for an uncomplicated camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guides are a youth organisation for girls; its youngest branch has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A young girl in the junior Guide branch, and an early cheap Kodak camera, share the name.

clue.text: Fish to cook on a barbecue

definitions.meaning: a trout-like freshwater fish
to scorch or blacken over heat

explanation.surface: Grilling fish outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout-like fish and the verb for scorching over flames share the spelling.

clue.text: Tried to get a seat. Unsuccessfully it would seem

definitions.text: Tried to get a seat. Unsuccessfully it would seem

parts.words: Tried to get a seat. Unsuccessfully it would seem
parts.note: a candidate who contests a parliamentary seat did so; someone who failed to find a chair remained upright

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to sit down but failed.
explanation.walkthrough: A candidate in a British election is said to stand for a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Contested an election, and literally remained on one's feet rather than sitting.

clue.text: Turn back the bolt holders and knock out

indicators.note: turn back tells us to read the word for bolt holders from right to left

parts.note: nuts screw on to bolts to hold them

explanation.surface: Instructions for loosening fixings before flooring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To render someone senseless with a blow is a synonym.

clue.text: Hyperbolic function which is a real stunner

definitions.meaning: the hyperbolic cosine in mathematics
a short heavy club for knocking someone senseless

explanation.surface: A maths function described as gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for hyperbolic cosine is spelt like a cudgel used to knock people out.

clue.text: A note added to a note suggesting recess

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Musical notes hinting at an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: It should be registered for a good job

definitions.text: It should be registered for a good job

parts.words: It should be registered for a good job
parts.note: valuable mail is sent by registered delivery, and a good job is a weighty position

explanation.surface: Advice to sign up for decent work.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighty letter needing registration, and also a prestigious appointment.

clue.text: Edward pursuing Charles X was beaten

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the Edward piece comes after

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward chases a king Charles and is defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles X' looks like a French king, but X is the Roman numeral ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbled or subdued, as one is after a defeat or punishment.
